deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is building a dictionary between several categories of combinatorial objects attached to arrangements of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. The previous page describes a 'cube' of such categories: oriented versus non-oriented, spherical versus projective, 2-dimensional versus 1-dimensional marked. This page treats the edge of that cube going from 2-dimensional objects to 1-dimensional ones.

1-dimensional arrangements (made precise on the next page). Take a finite 1-complex K with a family (D_i)_{i in J} of polygonal subcomplexes (the pseudo-lines) such that:
- every edge lies on exactly one D_i;
- two distinct D_i meet in at most one vertex;
- every vertex lies on at least two D_i;
- the D_i do not all pass through one point.

Octahedral graphs and their orientation. For every triple I of non-concurrent pseudo-lines, the union K_I of D_i (i in I), re-subdivided only at the pairwise intersection points, is the 'generalized octahedral graph'. Concretely it has 3 vertices, each pair joined by two edges. It is the quotient by the antipodal map of the 1-skeleton of the octahedron cut out on S^2 by 3 great circles.

This graph does not determine how it sits in RP^2. Choosing one edge from each double pair gives 2^3 = 8 triangles. These split into two parity classes of 4, and exactly one class consists of the 2-cells of the arrangement of the 3 pseudo-lines. Equivalently, at each vertex the cyclic order of the 4 half-edges can be either of two mirror-image choices. An 'orientation' omega_I of the octahedral graph is a choice of one of these two classes.

This page.
- An orientation of (K,(D_i)) is defined as a family omega = (omega_I) indexed by the non-concurrent 3-subsets I of J.
- If X is a combinatorial map ('carte', i.e. a 2-dimensional cell complex / map) which is an arrangement of pseudo-lines, its 1-skeleton K with its pseudo-lines is a 1-dimensional arrangement. It carries a natural orientation: the faces of X restricted to each triple select the class omega_I.
- This gives the functor (18): X -> (K,(D_i)_{i in J}, omega), from combinatorial 2-dimensional arrangements of pseudo-lines to oriented 1-dimensional arrangements.
- Claim: the functor is fully faithful, in the sense that Isom(X,X') -> Isom((K,D,omega),(K',D',omega')) is bijective. In words, the 2-cell structure is recovered from the 1-skeleton plus the chirality data on non-concurrent triples, and isomorphisms correspond exactly.

Purpose. This is a reconstruction step: the cell complex of a pseudo-line arrangement is encoded in a purely 1-dimensional, graph-theoretic object plus 'triangle orientations'. The next page sets up the characterization of which 1-dimensional data come from arrangements, presumably the essential-image question.
errors: 'Pleinement fidèle' is glossed only as bijectivity on Isom sets. Unless the categories are groupoids, this is full faithfulness of the induced functor on groupoids, not of the functor itself.

No proof is given on this page. The claim is plausible: the rotation system at simple vertices is fixed by the triple orientations. At points where three or more lines are concurrent, the cyclic order is not directly recorded by any non-concurrent triple. It must be recovered indirectly through lines not passing through that point, which exist by the non-pencil hypothesis. This step needs an argument that is not written here.

Minor: 'catégorie combinatoire 1 dimensionnelle des orientés de des arrangements' is a garbled phrase in the manuscript itself; the intended phrase is 'category of oriented 1-dimensional arrangements of pseudo-lines'.

ideas.what: Combinatorial (cell-complex / map) arrangements of pseudo-lines in RP^2
ideas.modern_name: Projective pseudoline arrangements as cell decompositions / combinatorial maps
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the notes themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Orientation of the 3-line 'generalized octahedral graph': choosing which parity class of triangles bounds faces (a mirror-chirality bit per non-concurrent triple)
ideas.modern_name: Local chirality / triangle orientation; analogue of rank-3 chirotope data modulo reorientation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroid theory: Folkman–Lawrence (1978), Bland–Las Vergnas (1978); Goodman–Pollack

ideas.what: Functor from 2-dimensional combinatorial arrangements to oriented 1-dimensional arrangements, with the claim that it is fully faithful on isomorphisms (reconstruction of the cell structure from the labelled 1-skeleton plus triple orientations)
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of pseudoline arrangements from local sequences / chirotope
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences); Felsner (local sequences); Folkman–Lawrence topological representation

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the reconstruction of a projective pseudoline arrangement as a fully faithful functor from 2-dimensional maps to 'oriented' labelled graphs. The orientation datum is a mirror bit for each non-concurrent triple, read off from the octahedral graph. The literature encodes similar data through chirotopes or local sequences, but not in this categorical form tied to combinatorial maps ('cartes', as in dessins d'enfants).
missed.quote: Le foncteur précédent est pleinement fidèle, i.e. pour deux arrangements comb. X, X' de ps. droites, on a Isom(X,X') ≅ Isom((K,(D_i),ω),(K',(D'_i'),ω'))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It places pseudoline arrangements inside Grothendieck's 'cartes' framework, where automorphism groups and isomorphism functors are central. The per-triple orientation viewpoint links oriented matroids to combinatorial maps. Mathematically, however, the reconstruction largely overlaps with known results.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially expected reconstruction statement, with close analogues in oriented matroid and pseudoline theory (chirotopes, local sequences). The novelty lies mainly in the categorical packaging and the link to Grothendieck's maps, and the unpublished pseudo-line project is itself of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'des graphes octaèdraux [?] correspondants' should read approximately 'des graphes octaédraux g[énéralisés] correspondants', with ω_I inserted above 'orientation'.

The functor's target is 'la catégorie combinatoire 1-dimensionnelle des orientés de[s] arrangements 1-dimensionnels' with an inserted 'et pr[ojectifs?]' / 'orientés' near the line end; a better reading is 'des arrangements 1-dimensionnels orientés de pseudo-droites'.
The beginning of the proposition is struck through ('Il y a un...', 'Prop.'), and 'Le foncteur précédent est pleinement fidèle' is the retained text.
The left-margin note is diagonal and partly struck through. Fragments such as '...vérifie...', '...qui...' and possibly '...bijectif...' are visible, but it is illegible overall.
